extraction.name: PASTIS
extraction.description: PASTIS is an open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series (SITS), with panoptic annotations of agricultural parcels. It contains over 2 billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km2.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot; Loic Landrieu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of satellite image time series for agricultural parcels with panoptic annotations, introduced as an open-access dataset for panoptic segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series (SITS).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-temporal satellite imagery / satellite image time series (SITS) of agricultural parcels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset includes panoptic annotations for agricultural parcels, where each pixel is assigned a class and a unique instance label.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper reports a limitation in the originally published panoptic segmentation evaluation due to a bug in the Recognition Quality metric computation, which artificially lowered RQ scores until corrected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and task are framed as having important economic and environmental implications, especially for agricultural subsidy allocation, crop rotation monitoring, and broader Earth observation applications such as urban development and deforestation monitoring.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for panoptic segmentation of satellite image time series, especially agricultural parcel monitoring, and is also used to evaluate semantic segmentation and panoptic segmentation methods.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and implementation are publicly available, and the paper documents a corrected version of evaluation results after fixing a metric bug, with additional details referenced in a GitHub issue.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images in sequences are embedded by a shared multi-level spatial convolutional encoder; temporal feature maps are collapsed into single maps using temporal attention and bilinear interpolation of attention masks across resolutions; Group Normalization is used in the encoder instead of Batch Normalization because acquisition times differ across samples.

name.evidence: We also introduce PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations.

description.evidence: Lastly, we present Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series (PASTIS), the first open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on SITS, with over 2billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km2.

creator.evidence: Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot Loic Landrieu

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “multi-temporal satellite imagery” and “satellite images” and “the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: "panoptic segmentation consists of assigning to each pixel a class and a unique instance label"; "we also introduce PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations"

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: a bug in the computation of the Recognition Quality (RQ) metric was present in the original implementation resulting in the void target instances not being properly ignored. Instead, all predictions matched to void target instances were counted as false positives, thus artificially reducing the RQ score.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: pixel-precise panoptic segmentation of agricultural parcels has major economic and environmental implications.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We also introduce PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations. We demonstrate the superiority of our encoder for semantic segmentation against multiple competing architectures, and set up the first state-of-the-art of panoptic segmentation of SITS.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Our implementation and PASTIS are publicly available. All models of Table 2 were re-evaluated with the corrected implementation. Refer to github.com/VSainteuf/utae-paps/issues/11 for more details.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: "each image in the sequence is embedded simultaneously and independently by a shared multi-level spatial convolutional encoder"; "a temporal attention encoder collapses the temporal dimension of the resulting sequence of feature maps into a single map for each level"; "we compute spatially-interpolated masks ... with bilinear interpolation"; "we use Group Normalization [50] with 4 groups instead of Batch Normalization [14] in the encoder"
